subject: research/milestone-schedules
professional: a contract theorist / mechanism-design researcher (relational contracts, limited enforcement), who would check the stage-game equilibrium conditions, the optimality argument, and the novelty against the relational-contracts and staged-payment literature

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (8 tests OK) and `experiments/run.py` (output identical to experiments/results.txt via diff). Recomputed with my own code (scratchpad ind.py, own stage logic by enumerating the requester pay/refuse and worker work/shirk nodes, own recursion R_k=(R_{k-1}-W)/(1+s)): (1) n*=17 at C=100,V=120,W=1; 42 at W=0.01; 37 at V/C=1.05; 5 at V/C=4, all match results.txt E1/E5. (2) pay-after needs 110, pay-before 25, best split 20 milestones at C=100,P=110,Wr=1,Ww=4: my stage checker flips infeasible->feasible exactly at 109->110 (theta=0), 24->25 (theta=1), and at n=20 the split is a knife-edge point theta=1-1/5.5 (a 1/1000 grid misses it, as expected with ties cooperating). (3) first milestone fraction 17.5% = 1-(C-W)/V = 1-99/120 = 0.175 by hand. The algebra c_k<=W+sR_k follows from F_r+F_w = W+(V-C)R/C, checked by hand. Outputs are right within the stated model.
evidence.completeness: README/paper claims checked: pooled condition c<=F_r+F_w (test_pooled_condition, passes); pay-after/pay-before/best-split counts (E3 reproduces); geometric schedule and closed form (E1, tests); first-milestone formula (test_closed_form_and_limit); entry-cost cap (E4); 2000/2000 and 10,000-draw search (E6 reproduces). Figure script and SVG exist. README says 3000/3000 stages vs a theta grid, which the test does (3000 draws). Paper section 3 claims the optimality of greedy by a monotonicity induction, written out. Paper cites no formal references (see claims). No stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: 8 tests pass. Seeded mutations in src/milestone_schedules/model.py, each reverted with git checkout: (a) greedy_schedule milestone x1.02 -> tests failed (2 failures, 1 error); (b) theta_range upper bound min(p,F_r)+0.05 -> 2 failures; (c) first_fraction denominator V->C -> 1 failure; (d) F_r in schedule_feasible multiplied by 1.1 on the (V-P) term -> ALL 8 TESTS STILL PASS (survived). The survivor is real: schedule_feasible only ever tests pooled feasibility for the largest-milestone path, so errors in how surplus is split between F_r and F_w (hence in the reported theta ranges) are not pinned by any test; E2's theta values are only checked by eye. The 'no shorter schedule' test uses 300 random cuts per instance; random cuts almost never land near the optimum, so it is weak evidence for optimality (the real argument is the induction in the paper). Tests recompute with the same model code rather than a separate reference.
evidence.craft: Read src/milestone_schedules/model.py (95 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py. Clean, documented, stdlib-only, deterministic seeds. Defects: n_geometric subtracts 1e-7 inside ceil (a silent tolerance that could undercount by one in a razor-edge case); stage_feasible and theta_range duplicate the same logic (the test cross-checks them, which is good); no input validation (W<=0 divides by zero in n_equal/n_geometric, P outside [C,V] or V<C silently accepted); __init__ uses star import; greedy_schedule has a silent cap=100000 that truncates the schedule without error.
evidence.claims: Every numeric claim in README and paper abstract is reproduced by experiments/results.txt or a test (17 vs 100, 110/25/20, 2000/2000, 10,000 draws, 3000/3000). Limitations section is honest (complete information, exogenous W, no discounting, optimality is within greedy-recursion and by induction). Weak points: the novelty framing cites 'relational-contract and self-enforcing-trade models' and Waggoner/Frongillo and Gensyn with no specific citation (no Baker-Gibbons-Murphy, Levin 2003, Halac, Watson 'starting small', Ghosh-Ray, Kranton), so 'the stage game is solved exactly' is unreferenced; the claim 'it does not matter who holds the relationship value' holds only for the best split and is stated so. README links the live page, I did not load it (not verified). No disclaimer needed for research.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can reuse the closed form and the stage lemma, but cannot build on it as a paper yet: no related-work section with real references, the model has exogenous W and a grim trigger so the headline 'logarithmic' result is a consequence of the pro-rata surplus assumption, and there is no real-data or protocol check (no comparison to an actual compute-market payment schedule, no verification cost). Nearest prior work: 'starting small' results (Watson 1999/2002, Ghosh and Ray 1996, Sobel 1985) already show that trust-building under limited enforcement grows exponentially/geometrically with stakes; Rosenthal-style and Shapiro-Stiglitz relational-contract milestone schedules; and the standard escrow-with-milestones literature. The geometric growth of stakes is therefore essentially the known 'start small, grow stakes' result applied to a specific stage game, which the paper partly admits but does not locate. Not at the PROGRAMMES.md PhD+ bar by itself: a small, correct note.
evidence.domain: A contract theorist would accept the stage-game backward induction (requester pays iff late<=F_r; worker works iff late-c+F_w>=0) and the pooled condition, which is sound in the stated model. They would object to: grim trigger with exogenous W instead of deriving W from a repeated game (the whole result is parametrised by an unmodelled constant); optimal-punishment and renegotiation-proofness are not considered (a grim trigger that forfeits all future surplus is not renegotiation-proof); no discounting inside the job, which the paper itself says favours big milestones and removes the usual start-small tradeoff; knife-edge ties resolved as cooperate; pro-rata value accrual means every partial output is worth its pro-rata share, unrealistic for compute jobs where partial output is often worthless. Math is right, model is thin.

defects.what: A mutation that scales the (V-P) term of F_r in schedule_feasible by 1.1 survives all 8 tests; the F_r/F_w split, hence the theta ranges printed in E2, is untested.
Novelty positioning without citations: the geometric-stakes result is close to the 'starting small' literature (Watson, Ghosh-Ray, Sobel) and relational-contract work, none cited by name.
Headline logarithmic scaling depends entirely on exogenous W, grim trigger and pro-rata value accrual; no real-protocol or data check.

No input validation: W<=0 raises ZeroDivisionError in n_equal/n_geometric; V<C or P outside [C,V] silently accepted; n_geometric hides a 1e-7 fudge inside ceil; greedy_schedule truncates silently at cap.
The no-shorter-schedule test samples uniformly random cuts, which rarely come near the optimum, so it is weak evidence; optimality rests on the paper's induction.

verdict: A small, correct, honestly-limited result: the stage lemma and the closed-form milestone count reproduce under independent recomputation (17/100, 110/25/20, 17.5% first milestone) and the experiment output matches the stored results byte for byte. It falls short of the bar on verification (one core mutation, the F_r surplus term, survives all tests, and the optimality check is weak) and on domain/fitness (exogenous W, grim trigger, no discounting, no citations to the starting-small and relational-contract literature that the geometric-stakes result closely resembles, no real-data check). Finished as a note; not PhD+ or publishable as it stands. Does not meet the bar because verification is 2.
